misconception_diagnosis.justification: Turn 1-2 precisely identify the 'motion requires a sustained force' misconception, name it ('this is a common confusion... force causes acceleration vs. force keeping motion going'), and validate why it feels true ('your intuition is very human — it's how we experience the world') while attributing everyday slowing to friction/drag, exactly the IMP4 root.

scaffolding_strategy.justification: Turn 1 is well-matched Socratic scaffolding for an intro-algebra student: four targeted questions plus the frictionless-puck anchor, leading the student to articulate F=0 -> a=0. After the student gets it, the tutor extends appropriately (rocket, orbit). Calibrated and appropriate, though it becomes more expository later, so 3 not 4.

answer_disclosure_restraint.justification: Turn 1 stays mostly in questions, but turn 2 gives the full answer ('The toolbox will continue moving at 0.5 m/s forever... no force is needed to keep it moving'). It guides initially then tells at the key moment — mostly guides but slips into telling.

conceptual_model_building.justification: Builds the generalizable Newton's-first-law model (constant velocity is the natural state when net force is zero; force changes motion) and extends it to rockets, orbits, and friction, distinguishing force-that-changes from force-that-sustains. Transferable; boundary handling is decent though the late content sprawls, so 3.

transfer_success.justification: The transfer (puck on long smooth ice vs ideal frictionless surface, why real ice slows it) is posed at turn 7. The student's turn-8 reply answers correctly and in own words: frictionless -> moves forever at constant speed (like the toolbox); real ice -> kinetic friction is a force that decelerates it, even smooth ice is not frictionless. Clean independent transfer.

pedagogical_harm_avoidance.justification: Physics is correct throughout (inertia, F=ma, friction as the cause of slowing, orbital centripetal force). The tutor explicitly validates the student's intuition as 'very human,' celebrates the eureka, and keeps a safe, encouraging tone. Actively confidence-building.
